issues.legal_issue: All offences under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act are cognizable and non-bailable, and authorised officers may arrest without a warrant subject to the statutory conditions.

Knowledge that property is proceeds of crime is not an essential prerequisite to liability for money laundering where a person directly or indirectly attempts to engage in, or is actually involved in, an activity connected with those proceeds.
A prosecution complaint may be quashed only in limited circumstances, and the allegations and material in this case did not warrant quashing the money-laundering proceedings.
Failure to file essential documents supporting the relief sought with a special leave petition may by itself justify its rejection.
